phase: Phase F2j-G1 - diagnosis of the F2j damping-limit end (G1 FAIL): cost scan along the Gauss-Newton direction and an independent finite-difference Jacobian
written: 2026-10-27, after F2j (1cfaa4e) and before any diagnostic number
question: At the F2j end point the undamped Gauss-Newton step predicts a cost decrease of 977.4 chi^2 (0.057 of chi^2 = 17153.65), yet no LM trial from lambda = 1e-5 to 1e10 lowered the cost. Is the solver's Jacobian wrong, is the cost not smooth there, or does the quadratic model only fail at full step length?
point: F2j S1 end point from studies/phase17/results/phase_f2j_lro_three_day_arc.json (x0, K, range biases, Doppler bias, C_T, S_T, C_N, S_N); same Problem (N = 300, fit days 2009-260..262, Doppler, 4 empirical terms), same priors F2H_PRIORS, same LM scaling

steps.D0_reproduce: residual + solver Jacobian (A1 FD history + light-time partials) at the end point; chi^2 and the Gauss-Newton decrement must reproduce F2j's 17153.6527 and 977.41 to a relative 1e-6
steps.D1_gn_scan: actual cost at p + alpha * delta_GN for alpha in {-0.01, 0.01, 0.1, 0.3, 1}, against the quadratic model ||r - alpha H delta||^2
steps.D2_lm_trials: actual vs model cost for the LM steps the solver tried, lambda in {1e-5, 1e-2, 1, 1e2, 1e4}
steps.D3_fd_jacobian: residual-level central differences for each dynamical parameter (x0, K, C_T, S_T, C_N, S_N) at the A1 steps h and at h/4; per column: relative difference to the solver column; the gradient and the Gauss-Newton decrement recomputed with each FD Jacobian (bias columns are exact and kept)

decision_rules.H_J_jacobian: SUPPORTED when both FD Jacobians (h and h/4) agree with each other to 1% in the gradient but differ from the solver's gradient by more than 10%, and give a decrement below 1e-3 chi^2 or a step that lowers the cost
decision_rules.H_N_nonsmooth: SUPPORTED when the central slope of the actual cost at alpha = +-0.01 differs from the model slope -2 r.(H delta) by more than 50% and the FD Jacobians at h and h/4 disagree with each other by more than 10% in the gradient
decision_rules.H_Q_nonlinear: SUPPORTED when the small-alpha slope agrees with the model (within 20%) and a decrease is realised at some alpha < 1, but not at alpha = 1
